title: hotfix(slo-enforcer): reduce aggressive shedding and add regional failover backoff
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: A production incident on 2026-02-19 exposed a regression in the SLO enforcer introduced by ENG-9077: under certain inter-region latency spikes the enforcer entered a thrashing state and triggered excessive load shedding for low-priority routes. Impact: customer-facing traffic saw 3-8% increased error/shed rates in eu-west and us-west for ~45 minutes. This PR is a hotfix to reduce aggressive shedding and to add a regional failover backoff (hysteresis) to prevent oscillation.  What this changes: 1) Tuned SLO enforcer thresholds: increase the shedding threshold by 15% for routes with <500ms p95. 2) Add hysteresis window to enforcer decisions: require a 30s sustained breach before shed is applied and a 60s sustained recovery before removing shed. 3) Circuit breaker decay: extend the decay half-life to 90s (was 30s) for regional failover counters to avoid rapid reopen/close cycles. 4) Regional failover backoff: exponential backoff with jitter for repeated regional failovers, configurable via config.sre.failover_backoff. 5) Metrics and alerts: emit slo_enforcer.shed_count, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_state and slo_enforcer.region_failover_backoff_active; add dashboard snippets and update alert thresholds. 6) Tests: add unit tests for hysteresis and backoff, integration test simulating cross-region latency spikes, and a small canary rollout config.  Why: The combination of a short decay window and immediate shedding caused the system to oscillate during transient infra latency. Adding hysteresis + longer decay + exponential backoff trades a small amount of responsiveness for stability and significantly reduces thrashing.  Backport: requests backport to release-2026-02 (will open backport PR after merge).  Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added - [x] Dashboard/alert snippets included - [x] Documented config knobs and defaults - [x] Manual canary performed in eu-west-1  Notes: this is intentionally conservative tuning to be safe during ongoing traffic; follow-up PR will add per-customer adaptive tuning once we validate stability.
